cards.text: This is a psalm of David, Israel's king, written for remembrance. David's talking straight to the LORD, and friend, he is HURTING. No small talk, no warm-up, he opens with a request.

cards.question: What's the very first thing David asks the LORD?

answers.text: Not to rebuke him in anger
To give him a long life

cards.text: David says the LORD's arrows have pierced him deeply and His hand has pressed down on him. Friend, that is NOT a little tap on the shoulder.

cards.question: David says there's no soundness in his body because of the LORD's ___, and no rest in his bones because of his own ___.

cards.text: His iniquities have overwhelmed him, and he says they're a burden too heavy to bear. His wounds are foul and festering, and he says it's because of his own sinful folly.

cards.question: David says he's bent and brought low. How does he spend his days?
Through all this, David says his body is finally starting to feel better.

cards.text: He's numb, badly crushed and groaning in anguish of heart. Friend, I know that groan, because I spent YEARS doing it into a takeout menu in the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: Right in the middle of all that groaning, David tells the Lord that his groaning is not hidden from Him.

cards.text: His heart pounds, his strength fails, and even the light of his eyes has faded. Hang in there with him, friend, because this psalm isn't over.
It's not just David's body that's hurting. Now he talks about the people in his life.

cards.question: With David this sick, his friends and family stay right by his side.

cards.text: Meanwhile, those who seek his life lay snares, plotting deceit all day long. ALL day long, friend, like they cleared the whole calendar just for this.

cards.question: With enemies plotting against him, what does David do?

answers.text: He acts like he can't hear them
He shouts right back at them
He makes plans to strike back

cards.text: David says he's like a deaf man who doesn't hear, and like a mute man who doesn't open his mouth. Friend, I've been in group chats where that's the WHOLE strategy.

cards.question: Even while he stays silent, David says the LORD will answer him.

cards.text: David had already said it: don't let the people who taunt him when his foot slips gloat over him. He's ready to fall, and his pain is always with him.

cards.question: Ready to fall, David says that he confesses his ___.
As he confesses, David says he feels at peace about his sin.

cards.text: Then David turns back to his enemies. He says there are MANY of them.

cards.question: What does David say about why his many enemies hate him?

cards.text: He says the ones who repay his good with evil attack him for pursuing the good. That's like bringing a box of cookies to work and getting WRITTEN UP for it.

cards.question: As the psalm comes to a close, what does David ask the LORD?

answers.text: Not to forsake him or be far
To wipe out all his enemies
To give him back his strength

cards.text: Now the very last line. David asks the Lord to come quickly and help him.

cards.question: David started this psalm asking the LORD not to rebuke him in anger. In his last line, he calls the Lord his ___.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says he spent YEARS groaning into a takeout menu in the junk drawer. His backstory says he gave up on himself only 'for a while' before the can opener pulled him out of his funk and he began welcoming every newcomer. The joke changes his drawer story, and the allowance for made-up moments covers only his bakery.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The setup line 'It's not just David's body that's hurting. Now he talks about the people in his life.' tells the baker that the people in his life are part of his pain. That rules out True on the next card ('his friends and family stay right by his side') before the baker answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer 'He acts like he can't hear them' turns the text's simile ('like a deaf man, I do not hear') into pretending. The text says he does not hear, like a deaf man. It doesn't say he acts as if he can't hear.
'David had already said it' adds a time ('already') that the text doesn't give, and 'it' points back to a saying that never appears earlier in the psalm. Verse 16 only says 'For I said.'

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The card calls David 'Israel's king', which comes from outside the passage, but it cites only Psalm 38:1. prep-walkthrough.md says outside facts like who a new person is come 'with their reference'. The card citation rule also says a story card cites the verses it tells, 'no wider and no narrower', and the JSON has a single verses field.
findings.question: When a story card introduces a new person with a fact from outside the passage (like 'David, Israel's king'), where does that outside reference go? Does it go in the card's verses field, somewhere else, or is it not needed for the simple new-person introductions in papa-dorin.md?
